_comment: Applied IN ADDITION to the primary boundary source, never instead of it:
where a place falls inside one of these territories, every claimant listed
is attested alongside whatever the source returned. The overlay is
deliberately additive — asserting that a source is WRONG about who
administers a territory is a far larger claim than asserting that more
than one party claims it, and WHG should not be making the former.
This replaces ccode_enrichment.BNDA_DISPUTED_CLAIMANTS, a hardcoded table
of four disputes which omitted Crimea, the Golan, Taiwan, Northern Cyprus,
Abkhazia, South Ossetia and the Falklands entirely.
Only territories with an EXPLICIT decision recorded below are included.
Disputes the primary source already represents by overlapping claims need
no entry: geoBoundaries HPSC returns both claimants for Gilgit-Baltistan,
Aksai Chin, Arunachal Pradesh and Taiwan without help.
Geometry is omitted where a polygon has not yet been sourced; such entries
are inert until one is added. They are listed so the outstanding decision

schema.name: human-readable territory name
schema.claimants: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of ALL claimants, to be attested
schema.primary_returns: what the primary source gives today, for comparison
schema.decided: ISO date of the decision, and by whom
schema.bbox: [minlon, minlat, maxlon, maxlat] cheap reject before geometry
schema.geometry: GeoJSON geometry of the disputed territory; null = inert

territories.name: Western Sahara
evidence: geoBoundaries gbOpen places Laayoune (-13.203, 27.154) inside MAR,
so 4,387 places would silently become Moroccan and no fallback would
fire, because the primary DID return an answer.
EH is a distinct ISO 3166-1 code precisely because sovereignty is
contested (Morocco vs SADR/Polisario). The `un` citation carries the
UN designation disclaimer verbatim — 'do not imply the expression of
any opinion whatsoever concerning the legal status of any country or
territory' — which asserting Moroccan sovereignty by omission would
Chosen as option 3 of three: return BOTH, consistent with how Kashmir
and the Kurils are already treated, and requiring no adjudication.
territories.geometry_source: BNDA EH polygon (un:esh), simplified to 0.01 deg with topology preserved; verified to still contain Laayoune. geoBoundaries does not carve out Western Sahara, so EH retains its BNDA outline in the `un` extract and this is the same polygon.

undecided.name: Kashmir (Indian-administered, Srinagar)
undecided.note: NARROWS from two claimants to one. Strongest candidate for an overlay entry alongside EH, since it runs directly against the stated all-claims policy. geoBoundaries DOES return both for Gilgit-Baltistan, so the inconsistency is within the source itself.

undecided.name: Golan Heights
undecided.note: CHANGES claimant. geoBoundaries follows de facto administration here, BNDA follows de jure.

undecided.name: Kuril Islands
undecided.note: Gains a code (BNDA returns nothing at all), but omits the Japanese claim.

undecided.name: Crimea
undecided.note: Unchanged; both sources follow de jure. Listed for completeness.

undecided.name: Falkland Islands / Islas Malvinas
undecided.note: Unchanged; both give the territory its own code.
